info.desc: So is the fifth studio album (and seventh album overall) by British rock musician Peter Gabriel, released in 1986. Many of its songs reflect a more conventional pop-writing style and became radio hits, others still retain Gabriel's dark, brooding sense of experimentalism. It is Peter Gabriel's second album produced by Canadian artist Daniel Lanois. The previous year, the two of them had worked together on Birdy. podcast.body: David Botrell worked as an assistant and provided some engineering support on this album, with Kevin Killing as the primary engineer. Botrell was present for the creation of songs like "In Your Eyes," "Red Rain," and "Sledgehammer." The recording process was described as "fascinating." "I was an assistant on that. I did some engineering and sort of helped out in places where they needed me."

podcast.body: Peter Gabriel extensively utilized sampling on his album "So." Although Stuart Copeland is credited with playing on the record, his contribution for many tracks was merely providing a snare drum sound, which was then sampled from an old Police record and used throughout the album. "Peter Gabriel did the same thing with his so-album."
